units.source_text: 众侍女口口声声劝小姐亲笔写信，小姐只得写了。

en.t: The serving women all urged the young lady again and again to write the letter in her own hand, and at last she had no choice but to do so.

units.source_text: 信笺是紫色的，但因历年过久，色泽褪损了。

en.t: The writing paper was purple, but after so many years its color had faded and lost its brightness.

units.source_text: 笔致倒很有力，品格只算中等，上下句齐头写下来。

en.t: The brushwork was quite forceful, though its refinement was only middling, and the upper and lower lines were written starting flush together.

units.source_text: 源氏公子收到了这封枯燥无味的回信，

en.t: When Prince Genji received this dry and flavorless reply,

units.source_text: 觉得阅读的勇气也没有，随手丢在一旁了。

en.t: he felt he did not even have the courage to read it, and casually tossed it aside.

units.source_text: 他推察小姐的心情，不知她对他的行为作何感想，心中异常不安。

en.t: He tried to imagine the young lady's feelings, and not knowing what she thought of his conduct, he was deeply uneasy.

units.source_text: 所谓“后悔莫及”，就是指这种情形而言的吧！

en.t: This, perhaps, is exactly what people mean when they say that regret comes too late.

units.source_text: 然而事已如此，还有什么办法呢？

en.t: Yet things had already come to this, so what could be done now?

units.source_text: 便下个决心：从今以后，永远照顾这小姐的生活。

en.t: So he made up his mind that from then on he would always look after this young lady's livelihood.

units.source_text: 这小姐却无由得知源氏公子的心情，在那里徒自悲叹。

en.t: But the young lady had no way of knowing Prince Genji's feelings, and there she grieved alone in vain.

units.source_text: 左大臣于夜间退出宫来，源氏公子被他劝诱，跟着他回到葵姬那里。

en.t: When the Minister of the Left withdrew from the palace that night, Prince Genji was persuaded by him and followed him back to Lady Aoi.
